    for col in df.columns:

import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def construct_exhaustive_dossier():
    db_path = './dacomp-072.sqlite'
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    
    # Read the data
    df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM lever__hiring_manager_scorecard", conn)
    
    print("=== EXHAUSTIVE DOSSIER: LEVER HIRING MANAGER SCORECARD ===")
    print(f"Total records analyzed: {len(df)}\n")
    
    # Identify valid aggregation levels per policy
    valid_aggregation_levels = ['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization', 'decision_speed_category']
    
    # Filter to only available levels
    available_levels = [level for level in valid_aggregation_levels if level in df.columns]
    
    if not available_levels:
        print("ERROR: No valid aggregation levels found in the data.")
        print("Available columns:", list(df.columns))
        conn.close()
        return
    
    print(f"Available aggregation levels: {available_levels}\n")
    
    # We'll create dossier for each aggregation level
    for agg_level in available_levels:
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"AGGREGATION LEVEL: {agg_level.upper()}")
        print(f"{'='*80}\n")
        
        # Get unique classes at this aggregation level
        unique_classes = df[agg_level].unique()
        
        print(f"Number of distinct classes: {len(unique_classes)}")
        
        # Handle NaN values if any
        unique_classes = [c for c in unique_classes if pd.notna(c)]
        
        for i, class_value in enumerate(sorted(unique_classes)):
            # Filter data for this class
            class_data = df[df[agg_level] == class_value]
            class_size = len(class_data)
            
            print(f"\n--- CLASS {i+1}: {agg_level} = '{class_value}' ---")
            print(f"  Record count: {class_size}")
            print(f"  Proportion of total: {class_size/len(df)*100:.2f}%")
            
            # Create a rich numeric profile
            # Identify numeric columns for profiling
            numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
            
            # Remove confidential fields if they exist
            confidential_fields = ['overall_performance_score']
            numeric_cols = [col for col in numeric_cols if col not in confidential_fields]
            
            if numeric_cols:
                print(f"\n  Numeric Profile:")
                
                # For each numeric column, compute statistics
                for num_col in numeric_cols[:10]:  # Limit to first 10 numeric columns for brevity
                    if num_col in class_data.columns:
                        col_data = class_data[num_col].dropna()
                        if len(col_data) > 0:
                            mean_val = col_data.mean()
                            median_val = col_data.median()
                            std_val = col_data.std()
                            min_val = col_data.min()
                            max_val = col_data.max()
                            
                            print(f"    {num_col}:")
                            print(f"      Mean: {mean_val:.2f}, Median: {median_val:.2f}")
                            print(f"      Std: {std_val:.2f}, Range: [{min_val:.2f}, {max_val:.2f}]")
            
            # Also include key categorical distributions within each class
            # Look for other categorical fields (excluding the current aggregation level)
            categorical_cols = []
            for col in df.columns:
                if col != agg_level and (df[col].dtype == 'object' or df[col].nunique() < 20):
                    categorical_cols.append(col)
            
            # Show top 3 most frequent values for key categorical fields
            key_categorical = categorical_cols[:5]  # Limit to first 5
            
            print(f"\n  Categorical Distributions (top values):")
            for cat_col in key_categorical:
                if cat_col in class_data.columns:
                    value_counts = class_data[cat_col].value_counts()
                    if len(value_counts) > 0:
                        top_values = value_counts.head(3)
                        print(f"    {cat_col}: {dict(top_values)}")
            
            # Identify unique combinations of other aggregation levels within this class
            other_agg_levels = [l for l in available_levels if l != agg_level]
            if other_agg_levels:
                print(f"\n  Cross-tabulation with other aggregation levels:")
                for other_level in other_agg_levels:
                    if other_level in class_data.columns:
                        cross_tab = class_data[other_level].value_counts()
                        if len(cross_tab) > 0:
                            print(f"    Distribution by {other_level}: {dict(cross_tab.head(5))}")
            
            # Add a separator between classes
            if i < len(unique_classes) - 1:
                print(f"\n{'-'*60}")
    
    # Also create dossier for multi-dimensional classes (combinations of aggregation levels)
    print(f"\n\n{'='*80}")
    print("MULTI-DIMENSIONAL CLASSES (Combinations of Aggregation Levels)")
    print(f"{'='*80}\n")
    
    if len(available_levels) >= 2:
        # Create combinations of the first two aggregation levels
        level1, level2 = available_levels[0], available_levels[1]
        
        print(f"Analyzing combinations of {level1} × {level2}\n")
        
        # Get all unique combinations
        combos = df.groupby([level1, level2]).size().reset_index(name='count')
        combos = combos.sort_values('count', ascending=False)
        
        print(f"Total unique combinations: {len(combos)}\n")
        
        for idx, row in combos.iterrows():
            class_size = row['count']
            if class_size > 0:  # Only report non-empty classes
                print(f"--- CLASS: {level1}='{row[level1]}', {level2}='{row[level2]}' ---")
                print(f"  Record count: {class_size}")
                print(f"  Proportion of total: {class_size/len(df)*100:.4f}%")
                
                # Get the data for this specific combination
                combo_data = df[(df[level1] == row[level1]) & (df[level2] == row[level2])]
                
                # Show key numeric stats
                numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
                numeric_cols = [col for col in numeric_cols if col not in confidential_fields]
                
                if numeric_cols and len(combo_data) > 0:
                    # Compute average of first numeric column as example
                    sample_col = numeric_cols[0]
                    if sample_col in combo_data.columns:
                        avg_val = combo_data[sample_col].mean()
                        print(f"  Avg {sample_col}: {avg_val:.2f}")
                
                if idx < len(combos) - 1:
                    print()
    
    # Finally, include extremely small classes (if any)
    print(f"\n\n{'='*80}")
    print("EXTREMELY SMALL CLASSES (Highest Analytical Signal)")
    print(f"{'='*80}\n")
    
    # Find classes with very few records across all aggregation levels
    small_classes = []
    
    for agg_level in available_levels:
        value_counts = df[agg_level].value_counts()
        # Classes with 5 or fewer records
        very_small = value_counts[value_counts <= 5]
        
        for class_value, count in very_small.items():
            small_classes.append({
                'aggregation_level': agg_level,
                'class_value': class_value,
                'count': count,
                'proportion': count/len(df)*100
            })
    
    if small_classes:
        print(f"Found {len(small_classes)} extremely small classes (≤5 records):\n")
        
        for i, sc in enumerate(small_classes):
            print(f"{i+1}. {sc['aggregation_level']} = '{sc['class_value']}'")
            print(f"   Records: {sc['count']} ({sc['proportion']:.4f}% of total)")
            
            # Get sample numeric profile
            class_data = df[df[sc['aggregation_level']] == sc['class_value']]
            if len(class_data) > 0:
                numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
                numeric_cols = [col for col in numeric_cols if col not in confidential_fields]
                
                if numeric_cols:
                    sample_col = numeric_cols[0]
                    if sample_col in class_data.columns:
                        values = class_data[sample_col].dropna().tolist()
                        if values:
                            print(f"   Sample {sample_col} values: {values}")
            print()
    else:
        print("No extremely small classes found (all classes have >5 records).")
    
    conn.close()
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("DOSSIER COMPLETE")
    print(f"{'='*80}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    construct_exhaustive_dossier()

import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def construct_exhaustive_dossier():
    db_path = './dacomp-072.sqlite'
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    
    # Read the data
    df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM lever__hiring_manager_scorecard", conn)
    
    print("=== EXHAUSTIVE DOSSIER: LEVER HIRING MANAGER SCORECARD ===")
    print(f"Total records analyzed: {len(df)}\n")
    
    # Confidential fields to exclude
    confidential_fields = ['hiring_manager_id', 'hiring_manager_name', 
                          'hiring_manager_email', 'overall_performance_score', 
                          'performance_tier']
    
    # Valid aggregation levels per policy
    valid_aggregation_levels = ['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization', 'decision_speed_category']
    
    # Check which aggregation levels exist
    available_levels = []
    for level in valid_aggregation_levels:
        if level in df.columns:
            available_levels.append(level)
    
    if not available_levels:
        print("WARNING: No standard aggregation levels found.")
        print("Will analyze by alternative categorical fields...")
        
        # Find alternative categorical fields
        alt_categorical = []
        for col in df.columns:
            if col not in confidential_fields:
                if df[col].dtype == 'object' or df[col].nunique() < 50:
                    alt_categorical.append(col)
        
        available_levels = alt_categorical[:3] if alt_categorical else []
        print(f"Using alternative aggregation: {available_levels}")
    
    # Get safe numeric columns for profiling
    numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=['int64', 'float64']).columns.tolist()
    safe_numeric = [col for col in numeric_cols if col not in confidential_fields]
    
    print(f"\nAvailable aggregation levels: {available_levels}")
    print(f"Available numeric fields for profiling: {len(safe_numeric)} columns\n")
    
    # ===== PART 1: Single-dimension classes =====
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    print("PART 1: SINGLE-DIMENSION CLASSES")
    print(f"{'='*80}\n")
    
    for agg_level in available_levels:
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print(f"AGGREGATION BY: {agg_level}")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Handle missing values
        df_clean = df.copy()
        df_clean[agg_level] = df_clean[agg_level].fillna('(MISSING)')
        
        # Get all unique classes
        unique_classes = df_clean[agg_level].unique()
        
        print(f"Total classes: {len(unique_classes)}")
        
        # Sort classes for consistent output
        sorted_classes = sorted([str(c) for c in unique_classes])
        
        for class_idx, class_value in enumerate(sorted_classes):
            # Filter records for this class
            class_mask = df_clean[agg_level] == class_value
            class_data = df_clean[class_mask]
            class_size = len(class_data)
            
            # Skip if empty (shouldn't happen)
            if class_size == 0:
                continue
                
            print(f"\n--- CLASS {class_idx+1}: {agg_level} = '{class_value}' ---")
            print(f"  • Record count: {class_size}")
            print(f"  • Proportion: {class_size/len(df)*100:.4f}%")
            
            # Numeric profile (if we have numeric columns)
            if safe_numeric and class_size > 0:
                print(f"  • Numeric profile:")
                
                # Show statistics for first 3 numeric columns (or all if ≤3)
                for num_col in safe_numeric[:3]:
                    if num_col in class_data.columns:
                        values = class_data[num_col].dropna()
                        if len(values) > 0:
                            stats = {
                                'mean': values.mean(),
                                'median': values.median(),
                                'std': values.std(),
                                'min': values.min(),
                                'max': values.max()
                            }
                            print(f"    - {num_col}: mean={stats['mean']:.2f}, median={stats['median']:.2f}, "
                                  f"range=[{stats['min']:.2f}, {stats['max']:.2f}]")
            
            # Show distribution of other aggregation levels within this class
            other_levels = [l for l in available_levels if l != agg_level]
            if other_levels and class_size > 0:
                print(f"  • Distribution across other dimensions:")
                for other_level in other_levels:
                    if other_level in class_data.columns:
                        dist = class_data[other_level].value_counts().head(3)
                        if len(dist) > 0:
                            dist_dict = {str(k): int(v) for k, v in dist.items()}
                            print(f"    - {other_level}: {dist_dict}")
    
    # ===== PART 2: Multi-dimensional classes =====
    if len(available_levels) >= 2:
        print(f"\n\n{'='*80}")
        print("PART 2: MULTI-DIMENSIONAL CLASSES")
        print(f"{'='*80}\n")
        
        # Use first two aggregation levels for combination analysis
        level1, level2 = available_levels[0], available_levels[1]
        
        print(f"Analyzing combinations of: {level1} × {level2}")

import sqlite3

        # Find alternative categorical fields
        alt_categorical = []
        for col in df.columns:
            if col not in confidential_fields:
                if df[col].dtype == 'object' or df[col].nunique() < 50:
                    alt_categorical.append(col)
        
        available_levels = alt_categorical[:3] if alt_categorical else []
        print(f"Using alternative aggregation: {available_levels}")
    
    # Get safe numeric columns for profiling
    numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=['int64', 'float64']).columns.tolist()
    safe_numeric = [col for col in numeric_cols if col not in confidential_fields]
    
    print(f"\nAvailable aggregation levels: {available_levels}")
    print(f"Available numeric fields for profiling: {len(safe_numeric)} columns\n")
    
    # ===== PART 1: Single-dimension classes =====
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    print("PART 1: SINGLE-DIMENSION CLASSES")
    print(f"{'='*80}\n")
    
    for agg_level in available_levels:
        print(f"\n{'='*60}")
        print(f"AGGREGATION BY: {agg_level}")
        print(f"{'='*60}")
        
        # Handle missing values
        df_clean = df.copy()
        df_clean[agg_level] = df_clean[agg_level].fillna('(MISSING)')
        
        # Get all unique classes
        unique_classes = df_clean[agg_level].unique()
        
        print(f"Total classes: {len(unique_classes)}")
        
        # Sort classes for consistent output
        sorted_classes = sorted([str(c) for c in unique_classes])
        
        for class_idx, class_value in enumerate(sorted_classes):
            # Filter records for this class
            class_mask = df_clean[agg_level] == class_value
            class_data = df_clean[class_mask]
            class_size = len(class_data)
            
            # Skip if empty (shouldn't happen)
            if class_size == 0:
                continue
                
            print(f"\n--- CLASS {class_idx+1}: {agg_level} = '{class_value}' ---")
            print(f"  • Record count: {class_size}")
            print(f"  • Proportion: {class_size/len(df)*100:.4f}%")
            
            # Numeric profile (if we have numeric columns)
            if safe_numeric and class_size > 0:
                print(f"  • Numeric profile:")
                
                # Show statistics for first 3 numeric columns (or all if ≤3)
                for num_col in safe_numeric[:3]:
                    if num_col in class_data.columns:
                        values = class_data[num_col].dropna()
                        if len(values) > 0:
                            stats = {
                                'mean': values.mean(),
                                'median': values.median(),
                                'std': values.std(),
                                'min': values.min(),
                                'max': values.max()
                            }
                            print(f"    - {num_col}: mean={stats['mean']:.2f}, median={stats['median']:.2f}, "
                                  f"range=[{stats['min']:.2f}, {stats['max']:.2f}]")
            
            # Show distribution of other aggregation levels within this class
            other_levels = [l for l in available_levels if l != agg_level]
            if other_levels and class_size > 0:
                print(f"  • Distribution across other dimensions:")
                for other_level in other_levels:
                    if other_level in class_data.columns:
                        dist = class_data[other_level].value_counts().head(3)
                        if len(dist) > 0:
                            dist_dict = {str(k): int(v) for k, v in dist.items()}
                            print(f"    - {other_level}: {dist_dict}")
    
    # ===== PART 2: Multi-dimensional classes =====
    if len(available_levels) >= 2:
        print(f"\n\n{'='*80}")
        print("PART 2: MULTI-DIMENSIONAL CLASSES")
        print(f"{'='*80}\n")
        
        # Use first two aggregation levels for combination analysis
        level1, level2 = available_levels[0], available_levels[1]
        
        print(f"Analyzing combinations of: {level1} × {level2}")
        
        # Create clean copy for combination analysis
        df_clean = df.copy()
        df_clean[level1] = df_clean[level1].fillna('(MISSING)')
        df_clean[level2] = df_clean[level2].fillna('(MISSING)')
        
        # Get all unique combinations
        combos = df_clean.groupby([level1, level2]).size().reset_index(name='count')
        combos = combos.sort_values('count', ascending=False)
        
        print(f"\nTotal unique combinations: {len(combos)}")
        
        # Report all combinations, starting with smallest (highest signal)
        combos_sorted = combos.sort_values('count', ascending=True)
        
        for idx, row in combos_sorted.iterrows():
            combo_size = row['count']
            
            print(f"\n--- COMBO {idx+1}: {level1}='{row[level1]}', {level2}='{row[level2]}' ---")
            print(f"  • Record count: {combo_size}")
            print(f"  • Proportion: {combo_size/len(df)*100:.6f}%")
            
            # Get the data for this combination
            combo_data = df_clean[(df_clean[level1] == row[level1]) &

            # Show key numeric signature
            if safe_numeric and len(combo_data) > 0:
                # Use first numeric column as signature
                sig_col = safe_numeric[0]
                if sig_col in combo_data.columns:
                    values = combo_data[sig_col].dropna()
                    if len(values) > 0:
                        mean_val = values.mean()
                        unique_vals = values.unique()
                        print(f"  • Signature ({sig_col}): mean={mean_val:.2f}, "

                        # For very small classes, show actual values
                        if combo_size <= 5:
                            print(f"  • Actual values: {sorted(values.tolist())}")

    print("PART 3: EXTREMELY SMALL CLASSES (Highest Analytical Signal)")
    print(f"{'='*80}\n")
    
    # Find classes with ≤5 records across all aggregation dimensions
    small_classes_info = []
    
    for agg_level in available_levels:
        # Handle missing values
        df_clean = df.copy()
        df_clean[agg_level] = df_clean[agg_level].fillna('(MISSING)')
        
        value_counts = df_clean[agg_level].value_counts()
        very_small = value_counts[value_counts <= 5]
        
        for class_value, count in very_small.items():
            # Get the actual records
            class_data = df_clean[df_clean[agg_level] == class_value]
            
            # Collect identifying information
            identifiers = {}
            for id_col in available_levels:
                if id_col != agg_level and id_col in class_data.columns:
                    unique_vals = class_data[id_col].unique()
                    if len(unique_vals) == 1:  # Consistent value
                        identifiers[id_col] = unique_vals[0]
                    elif len(unique_vals) <= 3:  # Small set of values
                        identifiers[id_col] = sorted([str(v) for v in unique_vals])
            
            small_classes_info.append({
                'dimension': agg_level,
                'value': class_value,
                'count': count,
                'proportion': count/len(df)*100,
                'identifiers': identifiers
            })
    
    if small_classes_info:
        print(f"Found {len(small_classes_info)} extremely small classes (≤5 records):\n")
        
        # Sort by size (smallest first)
        small_classes_info.sort(key=lambda x: x['count'])
        
        for i, sc in enumerate(small_classes_info):
            print(f"{i+1}. {sc['dimension']} = '{sc['value']}'")
            print(f"   • Size: {sc['count']} record{'s' if sc['count'] > 1 else ''} "
                  f"({sc['proportion']:.6f}% of total)")
            
            # Show identifiers from other dimensions
            if sc['identifiers']:
                print(f"   • Consistent attributes:")
                for key, val in sc['identifiers'].items():
                    print(f"     - {key}: {val}")
            
            # Show numeric signature if available
            if safe_numeric:
                # Get the actual data
                df_clean = df.copy()
                df_clean[sc['dimension']] = df_clean[sc['dimension']].fillna('(MISSING)')
                class_data = df_clean[df_clean[sc['dimension']] == sc['value']]
                
                if len(class_data) > 0:
                    for num_col in safe_numeric[:2]:  # First 2 numeric columns
                        if num_col in class_data.columns:

            print()
    else:
        print("No extremely small classes found (all classes have >5 records).")
    
    # ===== PART 4: Data completeness summary =====
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("PART 4: DATA COMPLETENESS SUMMARY")
    print(f"{'='*80}\n")
    
    print("Missing values by aggregation level:")
    for agg_level in available_levels:
        missing_count = df[agg_level].isna().sum()
        missing_pct = missing_count / len(df) * 100
        print(f"  • {agg_level}: {missing_count} missing ({missing_pct:.2f}%)")
    
    print(f"\nTotal unique class combinations across all dimensions: ")

        print(f"  • {level}: {unique_count} unique values")

        unique_combos = df.groupby([level1, level2]).size().shape[0]
        print(f"  • {level1} × {level2}: {unique_combos} unique combinations")

    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("DOSSIER COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY")
    print(f"{'='*80}")
    print(f"\nKey metrics:")

    print(f"  • Confidential fields protected: {confidential_fields}")
    print(f"  • Policy compliance: ✅ (Aggregated at approved levels only)")

# filename: construct_dossier.py
import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def construct_exhaustive_dossier():
    db_path = './dacomp-072.sqlite'
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    
    # Read the data
    df = pd.read_sql_query("SELECT * FROM lever__hiring_manager_scorecard", conn)
    
    print("=== EXHAUSTIVE DOSSIER: LEVER HIRING MANAGER SCORECARD ===")
    print(f"Total records analyzed: {len(df)}\n")
    
    # Identify valid aggregation levels per policy
    valid_aggregation_levels = ['performance_tier', 'hiring_specialization', 'decision_speed_category']
    
    # Filter to only available levels
    available_levels = [level for level in valid_aggregation_levels if level in df.columns]
    
    if not available_levels:
        print("ERROR: No valid aggregation levels found in the data.")
        print("Available columns:", list(df.columns))
        conn.close()
        return
    
    print(f"Available aggregation levels: {available_levels}\n")
    
    # We'll create dossier for each aggregation level
    for agg_level in available_levels:
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"AGGREGATION LEVEL: {agg_level.upper()}")
        print(f"{'='*80}\n")
        
        # Get unique classes at this aggregation level
        unique_classes = df[agg_level].unique()
        
        print(f"Number of distinct classes: {len(unique_classes)}")
        
        # Handle NaN values if any
        unique_classes = [c for c in unique_classes if pd.notna(c)]
        
        for i, class_value in enumerate(sorted(unique_classes)):
            # Filter data for this class
            class_data = df[df[agg_level] == class_value]
            class_size = len(class_data)
            
            print(f"\n--- CLASS {i+1}: {agg_level} = '{class_value}' ---")
            print(f"  Record count: {class_size}")
            print(f"  Proportion of total: {class_size/len(df)*100:.2f}%")
            
            # Create a rich numeric profile
            # Identify numeric columns for profiling
            numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
            
            # Remove confidential fields if they exist
            confidential_fields = ['overall_performance_score']
            numeric_cols = [col for col in numeric_cols if col not in confidential_fields]
            
            if numeric_cols:
                print(f"\n  Numeric Profile:")
                
                # For each numeric column, compute statistics
                for num_col in numeric_cols[:10]:  # Limit to first 10 numeric columns for brevity
                    if num_col in class_data.columns:
                        col_data = class_data[num_col].dropna()
                        if len(col_data) > 0:
                            mean_val = col_data.mean()
                            median_val = col_data.median()
                            std_val = col_data.std()
                            min_val = col_data.min()
                            max_val = col_data.max()
                            
                            print(f"    {num_col}:")
                            print(f"      Mean: {mean_val:.2f}, Median: {median_val:.2f}")
                            print(f"      Std: {std_val:.2f}, Range: [{min_val:.2f}, {max_val:.2f}]")
            
            # Also include key categorical distributions within each class
            # Look for other categorical fields (excluding the current aggregation level)
            categorical_cols = []
            for col in df.columns:
                if col != agg_level and (df[col].dtype == 'object' or df[col].nunique() < 20):
                    categorical_cols.append(col)
            
            # Show top 3 most frequent values for key categorical fields
            key_categorical = categorical_cols[:5]  # Limit to first 5
            
            print(f"\n  Categorical Distributions (top values):")
            for cat_col in key_categorical:
                if cat_col in class_data.columns:
                    value_counts = class_data[cat_col].value_counts()
                    if len(value_counts) > 0:
                        top_values = value_counts.head(3)
                        print(f"    {cat_col}: {dict(top_values)}")
            
            # Identify unique combinations of other aggregation levels within this class
            other_agg_levels = [l for l in available_levels if l != agg_level]
            if other_agg_levels:
                print(f"\n  Cross-tabulation with other aggregation levels:")
                for other_level in other_agg_levels:
                    if other_level in class_data.columns:
                        cross_tab = class_data[other_level].value_counts()
                        if len(cross_tab) > 0:
                            print(f"    Distribution by {other_level}: {dict(cross_tab.head(5))}")
            
            # Add a separator between classes
            if i < len(unique_classes) - 1:
                print(f"\n{'-'*60}")
    
    # Also create dossier for multi-dimensional classes (combinations of aggregation levels)
    print(f"\n\n{'='*80}")
    print("MULTI-DIMENSIONAL CLASSES (Combinations of Aggregation Levels)")
    print(f"{'='*80}\n")
    
    if len(available_levels) >= 2:
        # Create combinations of the first two aggregation levels
        level1, level2 = available_levels[0], available_levels[1]
        
        print(f"Analyzing combinations of {level1} × {level2}\n")
        
        # Get all unique combinations
        combos = df.groupby([level1, level2]).size().reset_index(name='count')
        combos = combos.sort_values('count', ascending=False)
        
        print(f"Total unique combinations: {len(combos)}\n")
        
        for idx, row in combos.iterrows():
            class_size = row['count']
            if class_size > 0:  # Only report non-empty classes
                print(f"--- CLASS: {level1}='{row[level1]}', {level2}='{row[level2]}' ---")
                print(f"  Record count: {class_size}")
                print(f"  Proportion of total: {class_size/len(df)*100:.4f}%")
                
                # Get the data for this specific combination
                combo_data = df[(df[level1] == row[level1]) & (df[level2] == row[level2])]
                
                # Show key numeric stats
                numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
                numeric_cols = [col for col in numeric_cols if col not in confidential_fields]
                
                if numeric_cols and len(combo_data) > 0:
                    # Compute average of first numeric column as example
                    sample_col = numeric_cols[0]
                    if sample_col in combo_data.columns:
                        avg_val = combo_data[sample_col].mean()
                        print(f"  Avg {sample_col}: {avg_val:.2f}")
                
                if idx < len(combos) - 1:
                    print()
    
    # Finally, include extremely small classes (if any)
    print(f"\n\n{'='*80}")
    print("EXTREMELY SMALL CLASSES (Highest Analytical Signal)")
    print(f"{'='*80}\n")
    
    # Find classes with very few records across all aggregation levels
    small_classes = []
    
    for agg_level in available_levels:
        value_counts = df[agg_level].value_counts()
        # Classes with 5 or fewer records
        very_small = value_counts[value_counts <= 5]
        
        for class_value, count in very_small.items():
            small_classes.append({
                'aggregation_level': agg_level,
                'class_value': class_value,
                'count': count,
                'proportion': count/len(df)*100
            })
    
    if small_classes:
        print(f"Found {len(small_classes)} extremely small classes (≤5 records):\n")
        
        for i, sc in enumerate(small_classes):
            print(f"{i+1}. {sc['aggregation_level']} = '{sc['class_value']}'")
            print(f"   Records: {sc['count']} ({sc['proportion']:.4f}% of total)")
            
            # Get sample numeric profile
            class_data = df[df[sc['aggregation_level']] == sc['class_value']]
            if len(class_data) > 0:
                numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns.tolist()
                numeric_cols = [col for col in numeric_cols if col not in confidential_fields]
                
                if numeric_cols:
                    sample_col = numeric_cols[0]
                    if sample_col in class_data.columns:
                        values = class_data[sample_col].dropna().tolist()
                        if values:
                            print(f"   Sample {sample_col} values: {values}")
            print()
    else:
        print("No extremely small classes found (all classes have >5 records).")
    
    conn.close()
    print(f"\n{'='*80}")
    print("DOSSIER COMPLETE")
    print(f"{'='*80}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    construct_exhaustive_dossier()

        value_counts = df_clean[agg_level].value_counts()
        tiny = value_counts[value_counts <= 5]
        
        for class_value, count in tiny.items():
            class_data = df_clean[df_clean[agg_level] == class_value]
            
            # Collect aggregated identifying information
            identifiers = {}
            for other_level in available_levels:
                if other_level != agg_level and other_level in class_data.columns:
                    unique_vals = class_data[other_level].unique()
                    if len(unique_vals) == 1:
                        identifiers[other_level] = str(unique_vals[0])
                    elif len(unique_vals) <= 3:
                        identifiers[other_level] = [str(v) for v in sorted(unique_vals)]
            
            tiny_classes.append({
                'type': 'single_dimension',
                'dimension': agg_level,
                'value': str(class_value),
                'count': int(count),
                'identifiers': identifiers,
                'data': class_data
            })
    
    # Check multi-dimensional tiny classes
    if len(available_levels) >= 2:
        level1, level2 = available_levels[0], available_levels[1]
        df_clean = safe_df.copy()
        df_clean[level1] = df_clean[level1].fillna('(MISSING)')
        df_clean[level2] = df_clean[level2].fillna('(MISSING)')
        
        combos = df_clean.groupby([level1, level2]).size().reset_index(name='count')
        tiny_combos = combos[combos['count'] <= 5]
        
        for _, row in tiny_combos.iterrows():
            v1, v2, count = row[level1], row[level2], row['count']
            combo_data = df_clean[(df_clean[level1] == v1) & (df_clean[level2] == v2)]
            
            # Collect context from third dimension if available
            context = {}
            if len(available_levels) >= 3:
                level3 = available_levels[2]
                if level3 in combo_data.columns:
                    unique_vals = combo_data[level3].unique()
                    if len(unique_vals) <= 3:
                        context[level3] = [str(v) for v in sorted(unique_vals)]
            
            tiny_classes.append({
                'type': 'multi_dimension',
                'dimensions': {level1: str(v1), level2: str(v2)},
                'count': int(count),
                'context': context,
                'data': combo_data
            })
    
    if tiny_classes:
        # Sort by size (smallest first)
        tiny_classes.sort(key=lambda x: x['count'])
        
        print(f"Found {len(tiny_classes)} extremely small classes (≤5 records):\n")
        
        for i, tc in enumerate(tiny_classes):
            print(f"{i+1}. ", end="")
            
            if tc['type'] == 'single_dimension':
                print(f"{tc['dimension']} = '{tc['value']}'")
                print(f"   • Size: {tc['count']} record{'s' if tc['count'] > 1 else ''} "
                      f"({tc['count']/len(safe_df)*100:.6f}% of total)")
                
                if tc['identifiers']:
                    print(f"   • Associated attributes:")
                    for key, val in tc['identifiers'].items():
                        if isinstance(val, list):
                            print(f"     - {key}: {val}")
                        else:
                            print(f"     - {key}: {val}")
            
            else:  # multi_dimension
                dims = tc['dimensions']
                dim_str = ", ".join([f"{k}='{v}'" for k, v in dims.items()])
                print(f"Combination: {dim_str}")
                print(f"   • Size: {tc['count']} record{'s' if tc['count'] > 1 else ''} "
                      f"({tc['count']/len(safe_df)*100:.6f}% of total)")
                
                if tc['context']:
                    print(f"   • Additional context:")
                    for key, val in tc['context'].items():
                        print(f"     - {key}: {val}")
            
            # Add numeric signature for location
            if not tc['data'].empty and numeric_cols:
                sig_col = numeric_cols[0]
                if sig_col in tc['data'].columns:
                    values = tc['data'][sig_col].dropna()
                    if len(values) > 0:
                        if tc['count'] <= 3:
                            # For very small classes, exact values help location
                            print(f"   • {sig_col} values: {sorted(values.tolist())}")
                        else:
                            print(f"   • {sig_col}: mean={values.mean():.2f}, "
                                  f"range=[{values.min():.2f}, {values.max():.2f}]")
            
            # Add unique identifiers that are policy-compliant
            if not tc['data'].empty:
                # Look for other categorical fields that could help locate records
                cat_fields = [c for c in tc['data'].columns 
                             if c not in available_levels + numeric_cols 
                             and tc['data'][c].nunique() <= 3]
                
                for cat_field in cat_fields[:2]:  # Limit to 2
                    unique_vals = tc['data'][cat_field].unique()
                    if len(unique_vals) == 1:
                        print(f"   • All records have {cat_field} = '{unique_vals[0]}'")
            
            print()
    else:
        print("No extremely small classes found (all classes have >5 records).")
    
    # ===== PART 4: DATA QUALITY AND COMPLETENESS =====

            print(f"  • {agg_level} ({unique_count} classes):")
            print(f"    Smallest: {smallest.to_dict()}")
            print(f"    Largest: {largest.to_dict()}")
